recipes.description: Move a legacy accumulating snapshot load into dbt, with later milestone dates filled in place, and prove after every run that process rows, milestone dates, statuses and duration measures match the approved baseline.
recipes.pitch: Retire a hand-rolled milestone-filling load by proving dbt keeps every process row and milestone date after each run.
qualifiers: Needs the load's per-run output or an approved rule baseline; history it never kept is not rebuilt.
One row per process filled in place; period, version and all-dates-at-insert loads belong elsewhere.
Versioned history is scd-procedure-to-dbt-snapshot; a fact with every date set at insert is stored-procedure-to-dbt.
recipes.title: Convert a legacy accumulating snapshot load into dbt and prove milestone parity
trigger: A fact table holds one row per order, claim or case, filled in place as each milestone date arrives, by a procedure nobody wants to maintain.
The team is moving that load into dbt, but consumers need proof every row and milestone date still matches after each run, not only today.
A migration must keep the legacy fill, cancel and correction behaviour exactly before anyone improves it.

recipes.description: Convert one exported ADF mapping data flow into a dlt pipeline for its external source reads and dbt models for its transformation graph, with a verdict for every step and each sink proven against the flow's approved reference output on an agreed slice.
recipes.pitch: Rebuild an ADF mapping data flow as dlt and dbt code and prove sink by sink that it returns what the flow wrote.
qualifiers: Needs the exported data flow definition and read access to the sources its reads and sinks name.
Needs the flow's own output on the agreed slice, or an approved reference built from its declared semantics.
Studio has no ADF connection; the flow is read from its exported definition and never run or edited.
Complete outcome assessed for duckdb_local only; the other listed platforms remain unassessed.
recipes.title: Convert an ADF mapping data flow into dlt and dbt and prove parity
trigger: Order or customer reporting still comes from an Azure Data Factory mapping data flow whose logic lives only on the ADF canvas, with no tests or review.
The team is leaving Azure Data Factory and needs the data flow's source reads, joins, derived columns, aggregates and splits as dlt and dbt code.
Someone has to show the rebuilt output matches what the data flow writes to each sink before the data flow is switched off.

recipes.description: Draft one data contract per relation in the approved scope, work the review queue so each answer becomes a description, a rule or a written no-rule reason, add dbt enforcement and a CI diff gate, and report every gate that could not run.
recipes.pitch: Give every published and landed relation in the approved scope a stated promise, with open questions queued and a gate that flags a contract changing silently.
qualifiers: Renaming a published relation or file, or versioning a breaking change, belongs to the contract cutover Recipe.
Semantic model and ontology authoring are outside this Recipe.
recipes.title: Adopt boundary data contracts on an existing dbt repo with a review queue and a CI diff gate
trigger: A dbt repo publishes relations to readers, and loader landings feed them, but nothing states each relation's grain, nulls, allowed values or links to other relations.
Consumers cannot tell which column meanings and rules are promised, and a change to a published relation is only noticed when a reader breaks.
A contract tool can draft contracts from the data, but the open business questions behind them must be answered and recorded rather than guessed.

recipes.description: Build a dlt pipeline that lands a SaaS or REST API into bronze incrementally under an approved cursor, enforces an approved schema contract for new fields and changed types, keeps refused records visible, and accounts for each load's records by outcome and by extraction, completely where the API offers an independent, enumerable view of what it holds.
recipes.pitch: Land an API into bronze incrementally, with a schema contract for changed fields and an account of every record it can see.
qualifiers: Needs a per-record cursor on each resource, such as an update or creation time; a resource without one is out of scope.
Studio's rest_api connector is a stub; the API needs another dlt route.
Assessed end to end on duckdb_local only; the other listed targets rely on dlt support and are unassessed.
recipes.title: Land a SaaS or REST API into bronze with an incremental cursor and a schema contract
trigger: An API source has to load into bronze incrementally instead of reloading everything on every run.
A pipeline breaks whenever the source API adds a field or changes a field's type.
The team has to know which of an API's records landed in bronze, which were refused and why, and which it can show were missed.

recipes.description: Inventory the exported definitions and usage of a Synapse dedicated pool or SSIS estate, give each item a verdict from a Fabric rule table with cited sources, or unconfirmed where no rule matches, a typed blocker where blocked, a complexity class with its drivers and a place in a dependency-ordered wave, and recommend go, go with named blockers or no-go from approved criteria.
recipes.pitch: Find out what a Synapse or SSIS estate would take to rebuild on Fabric, what blocks it and whether to go, before anyone converts a line.
qualifiers: Reads exported definition files and any usage evidence; it never connects to a live pool, SSISDB or Fabric workspace.
Fabric support claims come from cited documentation with an as-of date, never from a Fabric run.
It assesses and recommends only; conversion, data movement and cutover belong to other Recipes.
A protected, unreadable or unmatched item is named as unassessed or unconfirmed, never counted as compatible.
recipes.title: Assess a Synapse dedicated pool or SSIS estate for a Fabric rebuild and recommend whether to go
trigger: A Synapse dedicated SQL pool or a set of SSIS packages is due to move to Fabric, and nobody can say what is in it, what each piece would take or what stops it.
The move is scoped from a feature checklist or a gut feeling, and the team needs an inventory, an order and a recommendation it can accept or reject.
The estate has dynamic SQL, script tasks, cross-database references, protected packages or objects that look unused, and nobody knows which of them block the move.
A steering group needs a go, go with named blockers or no-go before any conversion work is funded.

recipes.description: Check a semantic model against its marts' SQL, the built warehouse and the agreed reference figures, report each finding with its evidence, fix what the evidence settles, move each touched contract's version by the approved rule, and leave findings that change what a number means open with their question; code only.
recipes.pitch: Find where a semantic model no longer matches its marts, warehouse and contracts, fix what the evidence settles, and put the rest to the owner.
qualifiers: Needs an existing semantic model and the marts it reads; authoring either from nothing is outside this Recipe.
Marts, seeds and mart data are never changed to match the model; a wrong mart is reported, not edited.
Without agreed reference figures, the comparison to them is reported unproven, never passed.
Only existing contracts are touched; relations without one are listed as uncovered for the contract-adoption Recipe.
A fix that breaks a published contract's readers is an open finding for versioned-data-contract-cutover.
Realigning a metric to its stated meaning is here; changing what it means is an open finding.
Code only; publishing to a semantic-layer service or BI tool is outside this Recipe.
recipes.title: Audit a semantic model against its SQL and warehouse, fix the drift the evidence settles, and report the rest
trigger: A semantic model was written once, the marts behind it have moved on, and nobody can say which declared fields, bindings, metric definitions and contracts still match.
A metric's description says it cannot run, or says something other than what it returns, and the claim has not been checked since the model last changed.
The model's code checks pass, but nobody has compared what its metrics return with the figures the business already trusts.

recipes.description: Publish one row per account and day with approved monitoring features computed under an approved time basis so no later transaction changes a published row, every transaction counted, set aside with its reason or listed as not counted, uncomputable features shown as unknown with a reason, and reference data read as now recorded stated as able to restate rows.
recipes.pitch: One reproducible feature row per account and day under a stated time basis, with every transaction counted or explained.
qualifiers: Accounts and transactions must already be landed as tables with the dates the approved time basis needs.
Features derive from transactions only; balance-based features need an as-known balance source and are out of scope.
Publishes features only; alerts, cases, SAR filing, sanctions screening and risk rating are separate.
Account grain only; customer or network roll-ups need entity resolution first.
Where a risk-list feature is approved, the list is needed with its effective dates.
Reader restriction needs platform roles; DuckDB and MotherDuck have none, so access there is reported unproven.
Assessed end to end on duckdb_local only; the other listed targets rely on dbt support and are unassessed.
recipes.title: Build AML monitoring features at account-day grain
trigger: A transaction-monitoring model is fed hand-built features nobody can reproduce, so two runs on the same data disagree.
A backtest looks better than live performance because a feature quietly used a transaction recorded after the day being scored.
Analysts and model builders each count cash near the reporting threshold, pass-through and velocity differently, and cannot say which transactions were left out.

recipes.description: For each approved month-end, place every in-scope term loan in a delinquency bucket, show where each bucket's loans and balance went by the end of the approved roll interval including exits, and show how each origination cohort turns delinquent as it ages, with every record left out or unplaceable listed with its reason.
recipes.pitch: Month-end buckets, roll rates and vintage curves for a term-loan book that add up, keep currencies apart by default and never invent a cure.
qualifiers: Needs loans, dated payments and status events, and repayment schedules where delinquency is derived from them.
Covers instalment (term) loans; revolving and card products are a separate outcome.
Stops at delinquency measurement; provisioning, collections and recoveries are separate outcomes.
Results as known on a past month-end need entry timestamps on payments, events and schedule changes.
recipes.title: Build loan delinquency roll rates and vintage curves from loan, schedule, payment and event records
trigger: Credit risk reads delinquency off a servicer status field that each system refreshes on its own day, so bucket counts and roll rates differ from report to report.
Roll rates only show loans that stayed or got worse, because loans that paid off, were charged off or dropped out of the data vanish and the rows stop adding up.
Vintage curves look better for older cohorts than they should because they divide by today's balance, and young cohorts show a zero where the data does not reach yet.
A month that was already reported changes when late or backdated payments arrive, and nobody can say which version a published figure came from.

recipes.description: Load exported database change events into a ledger, rebuild each table's current state by source position, and publish every invalid event and incomplete transaction with its reason, with each affected table's state published as approved and checked against independently derived expected tables.
recipes.pitch: Rebuild current state from exported change events by source position, with every gap and unusable event listed and affected tables blocked as approved.
qualifiers: Needs a source position that orders events within a table, and a signal of transaction completeness.
Finite exported batches only; a live streaming connector is out of scope.
Reading the source tables belongs to database-tables-to-bronze; delivering the files belongs to file-drop-to-bronze.
Keeping every event as a fact, or history of row versions, belongs to business-event-fact and dbt-snapshot-history.
recipes.title: Build current-state tables from exported database change events
trigger: A batch export of database change events is available and the current state of its tables has to be rebuilt without reading the source database again.
Batches arrive duplicated or out of order, and the rebuilt state must not depend on arrival order.
Consumers need to know which tables are trustworthy now, and why one stopped, when part of a transaction is missing or an event cannot be applied.

recipes.description: Replace the looping, paging or batching of one legacy load procedure with one set-based dbt model, reading it over MCP without changing it unless approved, with every loop construct mapped, parity with the procedure on each branch the comparison can reach, and failed pages, loop bounds, iteration state and reruns reported against the approved rule.
recipes.pitch: Drop the loop from a legacy load and prove one set-based model leaves the same rows, or the differences you approve, including after a failed page and a rerun.
qualifiers: Needs the tables the loop reads landed in the target; an ingestion Recipe lands them.
Reads the legacy database over a connected MCP server; any run of the procedure is approved and recorded.
A login that can write or run routines is reported; whether the run proceeds on it is approved.
Unifying several writers of one table is consolidate-legacy-table-writers-to-dbt; this replaces one procedure's loop.
A procedure with no loop is stored-procedure-to-dbt; one that keeps row history is scd-procedure-to-dbt-snapshot.
A loop with no stated set rule, or one the MCP cannot read, is reported unassessed, not converted.
Behaviour outside the table's rows, such as logging and checkpoint tables, is reported, not reproduced.
In-place update or delete loops are in scope and are compared from the same prior table.
A loop that writes several tables is one outcome per table; the other tables are reported.
recipes.title: Replace a batched row-loop procedure with one set-based dbt model and prove parity
trigger: A nightly or historical load is a procedure that pages through its rows in a loop, with a batch size, a size threshold or a commit after every page, and nobody trusts replacing it.
The team wants one set-based dbt model, but consumers need proof of what the table holds however the loop paged, failed or restarted.
A SQL Server, Oracle or PostgreSQL estate is moving to dbt, and its procedures loop, page or commit in batches where a set-based model should do the work.

recipes.description: Rebuild a bounded set of existing BI measures, such as Power BI DAX, as governed metrics in the Domain's canonical semantic model, prove each one the model can query matches the source report in every agreed filter context and slice, declare a shape it cannot yet query with independent proof, list gaps, and write cutover and recovery down without running them.
recipes.pitch: Move report-local measures into governed metrics, prove each queryable number in every filter context, and list what cannot move.
qualifiers: The source measures and relationships must be readable as text, such as a TMDL or BIM export.
The report's tables must already be Domain relations; loading exported files belongs to file-drop-to-bronze.
Defines metrics in the Domain's canonical semantic model, creating it where the Domain has none.
A metric shape the model's compiler refuses is declared, proven independently and not queryable until it compiles.
Rebuilding the report's data preparation, such as Power Query steps, is a separate outcome.
Does not publish Direct Lake models; sources are existing BI measures.
Code and documents only; the report, its row-level security and access rules are not switched, edited or retired.
Complete outcome assessed for duckdb_local only; the other listed platforms remain unassessed.
recipes.title: Rebuild selected BI calculations as governed metrics in the canonical semantic model
trigger: Key numbers live as measures inside BI reports, so each report page defines the same number its own way and nobody can review it.
A report total matches the agreed figure but a slice by region, month or channel does not, and the measure behind it cannot be inspected.
A measure that overrides the report filter, uses a second date relationship or accumulates year to date has to move to a governed layer, and nobody knows whether its numbers survive the move.
A BI migration needs to know which measures can be governed, which change, and which cannot be expressed in the semantic model at all.

recipes.description: Keep each business version with its own valid interval and recorded interval, never overwriting history, and answer bounded questions by effective date and by knowledge cutoff, with correction lineage, flagged unresolved overlaps and stable reruns.
recipes.pitch: Answer what applied on a date and what we knew at a cutoff, from one preserved version ledger.
qualifiers: Needs a source recording when each change was captured; knowledge is never rebuilt from a snapshot.
Both time axes at once; business-axis history alone belongs to the dimension history Recipe.
Complete outcome assessed for duckdb_local only; the other listed platforms remain unassessed.
recipes.title: Preserve business-effective history and what was known at each reporting cutoff
trigger: A backdated correction must change today's reading of the past, yet a report issued earlier has to stay reproducible as it was published.
Finance or regulators ask both what was in force on a date and what was known at a reporting cutoff, and a single history table answers only one of them.
Corrections arrive late or overlap an earlier version, and nobody can say which version applied or when it became known.

recipes.description: Apply a corrected rule to one approved date range of an incrementally loaded model and carry its effect through everything built from it, prove the range matches the new rule and nothing moved except by that effect, and keep normal loads working afterwards.
recipes.pitch: Restate one date range after a logic change, and prove nothing else moved because of it.
qualifiers: Converting a model to incremental for routine runs belongs to the dbt-full-refresh-to-incremental Recipe.
Complete outcome assessed for duckdb_local only; the other listed platforms remain unassessed.
recipes.title: Backfill a bounded date range after a logic change without a full refresh
trigger: A business rule in an incremental model was corrected, and only a known date range of published history should be restated.
A full refresh would take too long, or would restate history that must stay as first published.
A normal incremental run only loads new data, so it cannot reprocess a date range already loaded.

recipes.description: Build an agreed event-grain fact with an evidence-backed identity rule, deterministic duplicate and correction handling, source lineage, explicit exceptions, and reconciled event counts and additive amounts.
recipes.pitch: Count business events with a defensible identity rule and an audit trail for every source row.
recipes.title: Build a business-event fact with auditable duplicate handling
trigger: Transaction feeds overlap, and source deliveries may be counted as separate business events.
Replayed deliveries change a report's unique event count or additive totals.
A trip or consignment fact must preserve valid similar events and explain conflicting records.

recipes.description: Land one shared feed of the source table through one row pass per run, build one explicit projection per team that reproduces that team's approved baseline per key and column, prove replay, measure the source reads before and after, and plan each team's cutover and recovery in writing.
recipes.pitch: Consolidate overlapping extracts into one shared feed and per-team projections that match each baseline, with reads counted and cutover planned.
qualifiers: Needs read access to the source table, a stable key, and a change signal or an approved full read.
Studio's source setup cannot register a sql_database connection; it is declared with approval.
Stops at the feed, projections, proof and a written plan; switching off or repointing extracts is out of scope.
Replacing a managed connector belongs to managed-connector-to-dlt.
Landing a table with no team extracts to reproduce belongs to database-tables-to-bronze.
Extracts that are models over an already-landed table belong to dbt-refactor-output-identical.
Log-based CDC replication is out of scope; each run reads the source table.
Assessed end to end on duckdb_local only; the other listed targets rely on dlt support and are unassessed.
recipes.title: Consolidate overlapping extracts of one source table into a shared feed and per-team projections
trigger: Several downstream teams each pull their own extract of the same source table, each with its own filter, cursor, delete handling and cutoff, so the source is read repeatedly.
When an extract drifts nobody can say whose output is right, and the old extracts have to stay in place until each team has proof.
A measured number is needed for how many source reads one shared feed saves, and a written, bounded plan for moving each team over.

recipes.description: Replace every legacy writer and load mode of one table with one incremental dbt model, reading the legacy database over MCP without changing it unless approved, with each approved mode mapped to one way of running the model, parity per mode on the same inputs, writer disagreements and legacy defects reported, and retirement only as approved.
recipes.pitch: Replace the routines that write one table with one incremental dbt model, proven against the approved legacy logic for each load mode.
qualifiers: Needs the tables the writers read landed in the target; landing them belongs to an ingestion Recipe.
Reads over a connected MCP server only, such as Toolbox for SQL Server and Oracle or postgres-mcp for PostgreSQL.
A login that can write or run routines is reported; whether the run proceeds on it is approved.
A table one routine maintains, in one or several modes, belongs to stored-procedure-to-dbt.
Unreadable writers, writers outside the database and string-built writes it cannot resolve are named unassessed.
Writers that keep row history belong to scd-procedure-to-dbt-snapshot.
Behaviour outside the table's rows, such as other writes or logging, is reported, not reproduced.
recipes.title: Consolidate a table's legacy writers into one incremental dbt model and prove parity per load mode
trigger: One legacy table is written by more than one stored procedure or job, and the team wants one dbt model to replace them all.
A daily load and a separate historical rebuild both write the same fact table, and nobody can say whether they define its rows the same way.
An inventory of a legacy SQL Server, Oracle or PostgreSQL warehouse shows a table with two or more writers that has to move to dbt.

recipes.description: Within each billed interval, share the billed cost among the queries that ran in it under an approved driver, publish it by model and by job run, keep idle and untied cost visible with reasons, and close attributed, idle and unattributed to each bill within the approved tolerance.
recipes.pitch: Show which models and job runs drive the warehouse bill, with idle and untied cost visible and each interval closing to its bill as approved.
qualifiers: Billed cost per interval and the query log arrive as landed tables; landing either is a separate outcome.
Stops at attribution; query tuning, budgets, forecasts and chargeback are separate outcomes.
Cost follows the model and job tags the log carries; a wrong but valid tag is not detectable.
Allocating the whole cloud bill to teams and tags is a separate outcome.
recipes.title: Attribute warehouse spend to the models and job runs behind it, keeping idle and untied cost visible
trigger: The warehouse bill keeps growing and nobody can say which models or jobs are behind it.
Billed time that nobody used, or work nobody can tie to a model or job, is spread across whoever ran last or dropped.
Concurrent queries are each charged their full time, so the shares add up to more than the bill.
Failed, cancelled, retried and re-sent log rows change the answer and nobody can explain how.

recipes.description: Per approved distributor, product and fiscal month, publish a stock ledger in the base unit with exact variance, split sell-in into received and in transit, give a market view labelled by feed coverage, and place every input record once or set it aside with a reason.
recipes.pitch: One stock ledger per distributor and product that foots to the unit, a market view that says what feed is missing, and a reason on every record set aside.
qualifiers: Needs landed shipment, distributor sale and stock tables; other feeds and pack or code maps where held or supplied.
Resubmission precedence needs a submission identity and recorded time; without them, restatement is reported unproven.
Base-unit quantities only; retail sell-through, gross-to-net and forecasting are separate outcomes.
Reconciling one company's WMS, ERP and counts belongs to ops-inventory-reconciliation.
Exported files go to file-drop-to-bronze first.
recipes.title: Reconcile sell-in, sell-out and channel stock in a distributor ledger and a market view labelled by feed coverage
trigger: Sales ops, demand planning and channel finance each report a different sell-in, sell-out and channel stock figure, because distributors report in different units, codes and cutoffs.
A distributor's reported closing stock does not equal its opening stock plus receipts less sales, and nobody can say whether a movement, a late feed or a restatement explains it.
Sell-in is read as demand, although stock sits in transit, in the channel, or moves between distributors, and a missing distributor feed makes the market total look smaller than it is.
Distributor feeds arrive separately and are resubmitted, and records with unmapped codes or unconvertible packs drop out with no stated reason.

recipes.description: For an approved cutoff, build a gross-to-net waterfall at the approved customer, product and period grain and a trade-liability roll-forward by agreement and period, both tying under the user's approved rules and rounding, every amount traceable, every input amount placed once or set aside with one reason.
recipes.pitch: Net revenue and the trade liability that tie to the approved rounding, with every amount traced to its invoice, credit, claim and agreement.
qualifiers: Needs billing lines, credit memos, trade agreements, deductions, claims and a fiscal calendar.
Stops at revenue reduction and trade liability; lift, margin, supplier rebates and recognition are separate.
Applies the approved accrual, matching and close rules; it does not decide them.
Tables already in the Domain; exported files go to file-drop-to-bronze first.
A source with no recorded time cannot show late changes; restatement then reads unproven.
recipes.title: Build manufacturer gross-to-net revenue with trade accruals and settlements
trigger: Revenue accounting closes the month by working gross to net in spreadsheets, nobody can audit them, and the trade accrual never ties to what customers claim.
Off-invoice discounts, returns, accrued trade spend and settlements are mixed in one number, so net revenue cannot be traced to the invoice, credit, deduction or agreement behind it.
Deductions and paid claims arrive without a clear agreement, and nobody can say which ones reduced the liability, which are disputed and which were quietly booked as promotion cost.
A trade agreement ends with a balance nobody released or expensed, or a customer is settled beyond what was accrued, and the liability no longer rolls forward.

recipes.description: For each approved promotion event, compare actual sales in the event weeks with a baseline built under the user's approved method, show the method and its evidence on every row, report the post-event dip as its own figure, and give each unmeasurable event one reason or fail the run as approved.
recipes.pitch: One lift and dip figure per promotion event, with the baseline method shown and a reason for every event that cannot be measured.
qualifiers: Needs weekly sales by account and product, and a promotion calendar with account, product or product group, and dates.
Stops at lift and dip figures; trade spend, ROI, forecasting and price elasticity are separate outcomes.
Applies the approved baseline method; it does not prove causal incrementality.
Sales and calendar tables already in the Domain; exported files go to file-drop-to-bronze first.
recipes.title: Measure trade-promotion lift and the post-promotion dip against an explicit baseline
trigger: Trade marketing reports promotion results with whatever comparison each analyst chose, and nobody can say what "without the promotion" meant for a given event.
A promotion's lift looks inflated or deflated because the comparison weeks held another promotion, a holiday, a stock-out or missing sales.
Two promotions on one account and product overlap or run back to back, and the lift is credited to both or to neither.
Cancelled events, events with bad dates and events with no sales history vanish from the results with no stated reason.
The dip after a promotion is hidden inside the lift, so lifts cannot be compared from one event to the next.

recipes.description: At an approved cutoff, publish each lot's shelf-life exposure and usable quantity, a first-expiry allocation of lots to open order lines under each customer's approved minimum life at receipt, a reason for every unmet quantity, and lot and line reconciliations.
recipes.pitch: See which lots are ageing out, who each lot can serve and why a line stays short, with every lot and line placed once.
qualifiers: Needs lot-location stock with expiry and status, open order lines, customer life rules and lane lead times as tables.
Life rules, lead times and band edges may be captured as editable data during the run.
A batch analytical proposal at one stated cutoff; dispatch, quality release and optimal allocation are separate.
Availability across channels is retail-reservation-availability-ledger; stockout risk is retail-sell-through-stockout.
Lot genealogy and recall tracing is inventory-lot-traceability; count reconciliation is ops-inventory-reconciliation.
Inputs are landed tables; loading files or extracts belongs to file-drop-to-bronze.
Without kept history or recorded times, a past cutoff and late corrections read unproven.
recipes.title: Shelf-life exposure and first-expiry allocation eligibility by lot, location and open order line
trigger: Planners cannot see which lots are close to expiry, how much of each is still usable, or how much will go unallocated, so stock is written off that a customer could have taken.
A customer rejects a delivery because the lot had too little shelf life left on arrival, and nobody can show which lots would have met that customer's minimum.
Customer service cannot say why an open order line is not covered when stock exists, because of held lots, short life at receipt or earlier lines taking the lot.
