Every month-end someone rebuilds the deferred revenue roll-forward and cannot explain its movement contract by contract.
An auditor asks how much of a contract was recognised in each period and why, including after it was upsold, repriced or cancelled part way through.

recipes.description: For each approved scenario version, roll cash forward over thirteen weeks from opening balances and approved open items, payroll and commitments, keeping the date and rule behind every movement and every item left out of the weeks visible with its reason and amount.
recipes.pitch: Roll cash forward week by week for each approved scenario, with the date and rule behind every movement and nothing quietly dropped.
qualifiers: Open items arrive as landed tables; aging them is a separate outcome.
Uses approved assumptions only; it is not a forecasting model or a recommendation to borrow or invest.
Stops at the plan; budget comparison, revaluation and ledger posting are separate outcomes.
A past plan as issued needs kept snapshots; a rebuild restates it.
A calendar or rate the rules need but the source lacks is reported as unproven.
Rates, calendars and rules are inputs; sourcing rates and detecting duplicate invoices are separate outcomes.
recipes.title: Build a thirteen-week cash plan with traceable scenario assumptions
trigger: The weekly cash view is a spreadsheet rebuilt by hand each week, and nobody can say which receipt, payment or assumption moved a week's balance.
Treasury needs a weekly roll-forward for each approved scenario, with the date and rule behind every expected movement, before the cash review.
Overdue invoices, disputed items, undated obligations and invoices listed in two inputs are handled differently by each person who builds the plan.

recipes.description: Build the trial balance by account and fiscal period, plus entity and currency where more than one is in scope, with opening, debits, credits and closing, roll it up to statement lines, list late postings and invalid journals, and record each period's state at or after its hard close so any later change to it is handled as the approved lock policy says.
recipes.pitch: Rebuild the trial balance and close pack every period, with closed periods recorded, later changes caught and every journal accounted for.
qualifiers: Detecting a change to a closed period needs state that later builds and full refreshes do not rewrite.
Naming a changed line needs stable line ids; lateness and an as-at-hard-close record need posting instants and history.
Stops at the close pack; subledger tie-out, consolidation, FX and posting corrections are separate outcomes.
Assessed end to end on duckdb_local only; the other listed targets rely on dbt support and are unassessed.
recipes.title: Produce the trial balance and close pack as code
trigger: The close pack is rebuilt by hand every period and last quarter's trial balance cannot be reproduced as it was when the period closed.
Auditors ask what a closed period showed at its hard close and whether anything was posted into it afterwards.
Controllers need the journals posted after the soft close listed, and a hard stop when a closed period changes.

recipes.description: At the approved grain, assign each billing line to a team, product and environment by its tags, split shared pools by an approved method, keep untagged and unallocated cost visible with its reason, flag daily spikes, and close allocated plus unallocated to each invoice.
recipes.pitch: Show which team drives the cloud bill, with untagged cost kept as untagged and every allocation closing to the invoice.
qualifiers: Billing lines, invoices and tag rules arrive as landed tables; landing a provider export is a separate outcome.
Stops at the allocation; budgets, forecasts, commitment optimisation and chargeback are separate outcomes.
Currency conversion needs an approved rate source; without one, each currency is reported on its own.
Allocation is only as good as the tags and drivers supplied; a wrong but valid tag is not detectable.
recipes.title: Allocate cloud and platform spend to teams and flag untagged cost and daily spikes
trigger: The cloud bill grew and nobody can say which team or product drove the increase.
Untagged spend is unknown, or is quietly spread across teams so that no one owns it.
Shared platform costs are split by a rule nobody can reproduce, and the shares do not add back to the bill.
A daily cost spike is noticed only when the invoice arrives.

recipes.description: For each application and period, compare the seats the contract entitles, the invoice bills and the console assigns with the seats used under an approved activity rule, publish utilisation, unused-seat cost, shelfware and renewal timing, keep person-level idle seats restricted, and account for every record.
recipes.pitch: Measure paid SaaS seats against real use, flag shelfware before renewal, and keep the idle-user list restricted.
qualifiers: Contract, invoice, assignment and activity records arrive as landed tables; landing them is a separate outcome.
Stops at the utilisation report; renewal terms, deprovisioning and seat reclaim are separate outcomes.
Other plan models (usage-based, unlimited, pooled) need an approved treatment before they count as seats.
Past periods need assignment history of an approved form; a current-only export leaves them unproven.
Restricting the person-level lists needs roles and grants; without them the restriction is a label only.
On fabric_lakehouse, SQL grants do not govern OneLake reads, so restriction cannot be assured there.
Hiding small groups alone does not make a figure safe to release; totals and sibling cells can reveal one.
Unless issued periods are kept as retained copies, a late or backdated event restates the periods it affects.
Vendor activity feeds differ; unless approved otherwise, no feed or a declared gap reads unknown, not inactive.
Assessed end to end on duckdb_local only; the other listed targets rely on dbt support and are unassessed.
recipes.title: Measure SaaS licence utilisation and shelfware against contracts and invoices
trigger: A SaaS renewal is due and nobody can say how many of the paid seats are actually used.
The vendor console, the contract and the invoice show different seat counts for the same application.
Finance is asked what the unused seats cost and which applications are shelfware before the renewal date.

recipes.description: Define the approved metrics once in a governed Ossie semantic model over a gold fact mart, prove that what the model returns for each metric it can compile equals an independent computation of the approved definition, keep a refused shape as an independent value, and reconcile to the agreed reference figures, every difference named and sized; code only.
recipes.pitch: Define each metric once, prove its numbers, and name and size every difference from the agreed reference figures.
qualifiers: Needs a gold fact mart with a declared grain; changing marts or building a new fact mart is outside this Recipe.
A metric population that reads another dimension's attribute cannot be stated in the model today; see Ask first.
A shape the compiler refuses is reported with its refusal and an independent value, not queried.
Code only; publishing to a semantic-layer service or BI tool is outside this Recipe.
Migrating existing BI measures belongs to bi-calculations-to-governed-metrics.
A metric built as a materialised table belongs to metric-population-and-rollups.
recipes.title: Define governed metrics once in the Domain's semantic model over a gold fact and prove their values
trigger: Revenue or average order value means different things in different marts and dashboards, and nobody can say which number is right.
Each new report re-implements the same KPI in SQL with its own filters, and the copies drift apart.
A rate gives a different answer by day than by month because copies aggregate it differently.
Analysts need agreed metrics they can slice by agreed dimensions and periods without knowing the joins.

recipes.description: Build a dlt pipeline and a governed table that load each new export of a hand-maintained spreadsheet under an approved structure contract, keep the last accepted version live when an export breaks it, set aside bad rows with reasons, retain accepted versions as approved, and document every column with its owner.
recipes.pitch: Turn the spreadsheet everyone depends on into a governed table that fails loudly when its structure breaks.
qualifiers: Needs a Studio route for dlt to read the file; cloud buckets (ADLS, S3) have none today.
A recurring feed of delivered files that state their own completeness is file-drop-to-bronze.
Each export must be a full copy of the sheet; a partial extract or change feed is out of scope.
Covers a delimited text export such as CSV; reading a workbook directly is out of scope.
Sized for spreadsheet-scale files, not large extracts.
Assessed end to end on duckdb_local only; the other listed targets rely on dlt support and are unassessed.
recipes.title: Promote a spreadsheet or CSV to a governed, tested table
trigger: A spreadsheet that reports and models depend on is edited by hand, and a moved, renamed or retyped column keeps breaking them quietly.
Nobody can say what each column of a hand-maintained file means, who owns it or which row is the key.
A team keeps editing a sheet and re-exporting it, and wants a warehouse table of it that is checked on every new export.

recipes.description: Explain every billed claim line as paid, adjusted, patient responsibility, denied or open so the pieces add up to the billed amount, summarise the same by payer with denial rate and denial reasons, account for every remittance line as applied or set aside with its reason, and tie each remittance batch to its payment.
recipes.pitch: Billed to paid, adjusted, denied and open for every claim line and payer, with every remittance line applied or explained and every batch tied to its payment.
qualifiers: Claims, remittance lines and batch payments must be landed; reason-code rules may be captured as editable data.
Stops at the reconciliation; appeals, resubmission, underpayment checks, patient billing and bank matching are separate.
Only as complete as the remittances received; claims not yet remitted are shown as approved.
recipes.title: Reconcile billed claims to payer remittances, denials and batch payments by payer
trigger: The revenue cycle team matches payer remittances to billed claims by hand, and nobody can say, payer by payer, how much of what was billed was paid, adjusted, denied or is still open.
A payer's denial rate or top denial reasons are quoted from a spreadsheet that mixes claim-level and line-level amounts, counts a resent remittance twice or reads patient responsibility as a denial.
A remittance batch does not match the payment it carries, a remittance names a claim nobody holds, or a billed claim has no remittance yet, and the gap is found only at month end.

recipes.description: Classify every loaded admission as an eligible index admission, an admission excluded for one named reason, or an admission set aside as unusable, link each eligible index to the admission that readmits it, and publish a readmission rate by facility and month that ties back to the cohort.
recipes.pitch: Every admission is an index, excluded for a stated reason or set aside, and the readmission rate ties back to it.
qualifiers: Admissions with patient, facility, dates, type, outcome and planned flag must already be landed as a table.
Stops at the cohort and rate; risk adjustment, cost, root cause and outreach are separate.
Readmissions to facilities missing from the data cannot be seen, and are not claimed absent.
recipes.title: Build a thirty-day readmission cohort with explicit exclusions
trigger: The quality team rebuilds a readmission rate from a spreadsheet each quarter, and nobody can say who was left out of the rate or why.
Readmissions come from a self-join, so a patient with several returns is counted twice, a planned return counts against the hospital or a return to another facility is missed.
Deaths, transfers, discharges against medical advice and discharges too recent to have had a full follow-up window sit in the rate, or vanish from it without a trace.

recipes.description: Publish rooms available, sold and occupied, room revenue, occupancy, ADR and RevPAR per property and night from reservation lines and room inventory, with every line counted or set aside with a reason and amendments to closed nights handled visibly as approved.
recipes.pitch: One nightly table of occupancy, ADR and RevPAR that reconciles to every reservation line and rolls up from sums.
qualifiers: Needs reservation lines with a nightly rate and a room inventory per property and night already landed as tables.
Stops at the nightly table; forecasting, pace, comp-set index, channel mix and profit measures are separate work.
Judging a later amendment needs a close per night, from the source or an approved rule.
recipes.title: Build nightly occupancy, ADR and RevPAR by property with closed-night restatements
trigger: Occupancy, ADR and RevPAR differ between reports because each one counts stays, comps, out-of-order rooms and cancellations its own way.
A multi-night stay lands on its check-in day, the checkout day is counted as a night, or a month's ADR is an average of daily ADRs.
A reservation amended after a night closed quietly changes a morning figure that revenue management already acted on.

recipes.description: Resolve customer records from several source systems into one golden record per customer, with a two-way crosswalk, approved match and survivorship rules held as data, golden ids that stay stable across runs, an unresolved list that accounts for every source record, and an optional comparison with a source system's own merge pointers.
recipes.pitch: One customer, one stable id, every source record traced to it and every unresolved one explained.
qualifiers: Expects names and addresses already standardized, with a match key, by an earlier standardization step.
Stable golden ids need the id register to persist between runs; a rebuild from scratch reissues them.
Without retained crosswalk history, the crosswalk as it stood on a past run cannot be reconstructed.
Complete outcome assessed for duckdb_local only; the other listed platforms remain unassessed.
recipes.title: Deduplicate customers into a golden record with a source crosswalk
trigger: The same customer exists in several systems under different ids, so customer counts and per-customer revenue are inflated.
Analysts need to trace a golden customer to every source record behind it, and any source record to its golden customer.
Source systems disagree on a customer's name, address or contact details and nobody can say which value wins or why.
Customer ids change from one run to the next when a later record turns out to belong to an existing customer.

recipes.description: Standardize every source record's name and postal address under approved, editable rules, keep the original values beside the standardized ones, mint deterministic match keys that agree exactly when the standardized values agree, and account for every record as standardized or excluded with a reason, without merging records.
recipes.pitch: Give every customer record a clean name, a clean address and a match key you can explain.
qualifiers: Addresses are standardized by rule, not verified against a postal service, so deliverability is not checked.
Complete outcome assessed for duckdb_local only; the other listed platforms remain unassessed.
recipes.title: Standardize names and addresses and mint deterministic match keys
trigger: The same customer is written differently across CRM, billing and support, so joins on name or address miss.
A deduplication or golden-record step needs stable, explainable match keys before any fuzzy matching.
Addresses arrive in mixed formats across countries, so reports group the same address several ways.
Match results must be reproducible from run to run, without depending on run order or an external service.

recipes.description: Author a new incremental dbt model with an enforced output contract, then prove that a rerun and a re-delivery of records already applied leave it unchanged under the approved definition, with records the approved rules set aside kept visible.
recipes.pitch: Build an incremental dbt model with an enforced contract and show that a rerun or a re-delivery of records already applied leaves it unchanged.
qualifiers: Needs a source that carries a key and a version or update timestamp for each record, and can be read in full.
Converting an existing full-refresh model belongs to the dbt-full-refresh-to-incremental Recipe.
Assessed end to end on duckdb_local only; the other listed targets rely on dbt support and are unassessed.
recipes.title: Author an incremental dbt model with its contract and prove idempotency
trigger: A new dbt model must be brought up to date incrementally on each run, and nobody can show that a rerun or a re-delivery of records already applied leaves it unchanged.
Downstream consumers need a guaranteed set of columns, types and keys, and a build should fail when the output drifts from them.
A loader resends or corrects records, and the table must stay correct when the same batch is delivered twice.

recipes.description: Publish paid and incurred loss triangles by accident period and development age, one per segment, each cell as known at its evaluation date, with every claim transaction counted in a cell or set aside with its reason and the totals tied back to the inputs.
recipes.pitch: Reproducible paid and incurred triangles whose older diagonals never move, with every claim transaction counted or explained.
qualifiers: Claims and claim transactions must already be landed as tables with the dates the approved time basis needs.
Amount triangles only; claim counts, factors, IBNR, ultimates, reserving and reinsurance cessions are separate.
Results are only as complete as the transaction history the source carries; earlier history is not recoverable here.
recipes.title: Build paid and incurred claims loss triangles by accident and development period
trigger: Reserving analysts rebuild loss triangles by hand in spreadsheets, and a late payment or reserve change pushes back into cells that were already reported.
Two runs of the same claims data give different older diagonals, so development methods run on numbers nobody can reproduce.
Incurred is read with today's case reserve instead of the reserve as it stood at each evaluation date, and nobody can say which claim transactions a triangle left out.

recipes.description: Read a legacy SQL Server, Oracle or PostgreSQL database through its connected MCP, report its objects, call graph, table writers and profile without changing the source, then plan its migration by units, order and what each object becomes.
recipes.pitch: Find out what a legacy database holds, who calls and writes what, and what its data looks like, then get a saved plan for migrating it.
qualifiers: Reads over a connected MCP server only, such as Toolbox for SQL Server and Oracle or postgres-mcp for PostgreSQL.
A login that can write or run routines is reported; whether the run proceeds on it is approved.
Exported definition files are out of scope; a Synapse or SSIS estate bound for Fabric is assess-synapse-ssis-for-fabric.
It profiles tables to understand them, not to reconcile a load, which database-tables-to-bronze covers.
Planning stops at an approved plan; converting objects and loading are other Recipes.
Writers outside the database, and objects the login cannot read, are named unassessed.
recipes.title: Inventory a legacy SQL Server, Oracle or PostgreSQL database over MCP and plan its migration
trigger: A legacy SQL Server, Oracle or PostgreSQL database is due to be re-engineered and nobody can say which routines call which, or which objects write each table.
A set of stored routines has to be planned object by object, and the plan needs the objects, callers, writers and the shape of the data first.
The estate has dynamic SQL, nested calls, tables with two writers or objects nothing calls, and the team needs them found before any conversion starts.

recipes.description: From observed receipts, production runs that consume and make lots, and shipments, build the lot genealogy with quantities and units on each link, and for a recalled lot list every affected lot and shipment once with the recalled quantity, with unreconciled runs, cycles and untraceable shipments shown.
recipes.pitch: Trace a recalled lot to every affected shipment once, and show unreconciled runs and shipments whose history cannot be followed.
qualifiers: Needs observed genealogy, such as lots consumed and produced per run; links are never inferred from dates.
Lots follow one identification scheme; mapping between schemes is a separate outcome.
Inputs are landed tables; loading files or extracts belongs to file-drop-to-bronze.
Stops at recall exposure evidence; notifying customers and the physical recall are separate outcomes.
Stock positions and product hierarchies belong to ops-inventory-reconciliation and master-product-sku-hierarchy.
recipes.title: Trace a recalled input lot to affected shipments and flag unreconciled runs and lineage that cannot be traced
trigger: A raw material lot is recalled and nobody can say which finished lots and which customer shipments contain it, or how much of it each holds.
Lot genealogy lives in spreadsheets or separate receipt, production and shipping systems, and a split or blend makes the same material reach a shipment by several routes.
A mock recall must show every affected shipment, and every shipment whose history cannot be followed.

recipes.description: Under one approved costing policy and reporting currency, value each stock movement in a ledger, publish closing stock and cost of goods sold by approved period, keep quantity and value conserved, and list what cannot be valued instead of costing it at zero.
recipes.pitch: Value every stock movement and cost of goods sold under one approved costing policy, with no missing cost quietly becoming zero.
qualifiers: Inputs are landed stock-movement tables; loading files or extracts belongs to file-drop-to-bronze.
One costing policy and one reporting currency per run; currency conversion is upstream work.
Stops at valued inventory and COGS; counts, stockout risk and ledger posting are separate outcomes.
Restating for a backdated movement needs an entry or posting time on each movement; without it restatement is unproven.
Net realisable value write-downs are a separate outcome.
recipes.title: Value inventory movements, closing stock and cost of goods sold under an approved costing policy
trigger: Finance cannot say what closing inventory is worth or how much cost of goods sold a month carries because receipts, issues, returns and adjustments are costed by hand.
A late or backdated receipt arrives and nobody can say which issues, periods and cost figures it changes.
The books are about to close and a missing cost, a return or an issue beyond stock on hand has quietly become zero in the valuation.

recipes.description: Move one legacy fact load's dimension-key resolution into dbt, read over MCP without changing the legacy unless approved, with late and unseen-member lines landing as the approved rule gives, every staged line published or listed once with its approved reason, and a set-aside line placed once its member arrives.
recipes.pitch: Prove a dbt fact puts late and unseen-member lines where the legacy load did, with each line it cannot place listed with its reason.
qualifiers: Needs the fact's inputs and dimensions landed in the target; an ingestion Recipe lands them.
Reads over a connected MCP server, such as Toolbox for SQL Server and Oracle or postgres-mcp for PostgreSQL.
Any run of a legacy routine is approved and recorded; a login that can write or run routines is reported.
Several writers of one table is consolidate-legacy-table-writers-to-dbt.
A paging loop is batched-loop-procedure-to-set-based-dbt; a load with no dimension lookup is stored-procedure-to-dbt.
Keeping dimension history is scd-procedure-to-dbt-snapshot; replayed deliveries belong to business-event-fact.
A lookup the MCP cannot read is reported unassessed, not converted.
Behaviour outside the fact's rows, such as logging, is reported, not reproduced.
recipes.title: Resolve late-arriving facts and unseen dimension members in a dbt fact and list every line it cannot place
trigger: A legacy fact load looks up dimension keys, and a line that arrives late or names a member never seen lands on a key nobody can explain, or vanishes.
The load is moving to dbt, and consumers need proof that late lines and unseen-member lines land where the legacy load put them, or are shown with a reason.
A SQL Server, Oracle or PostgreSQL fact load moves to dbt, and a line set aside for a missing member must be placed once it arrives, with loaded rows undisturbed.

recipes.description: Replace a legacy periodic snapshot load, one row per entity per period, with a dbt model, and prove after every compared run that each period matches the approved legacy result, including the migrated history, a missing period, a rerun, a correction and later runs that change earlier periods.
recipes.pitch: Move a legacy period-by-period snapshot into dbt and show every period still matches after each run.
qualifiers: Needs the job's definition and its run record, or inputs from which its runs can be replayed.
Needs the tables the job reads landed in the target; landing them belongs to an ingestion Recipe.
A job that only keeps the version history of an entity belongs to scd-procedure-to-dbt-snapshot.
A new append-only snapshot with no legacy job to match belongs to revops-pipeline-snapshots.
A routine that maintains a table with no period grain belongs to stored-procedure-to-dbt.
Full-rebuild views and tables with several writers go to legacy-sql-to-dbt and consolidate-legacy-table-writers-to-dbt.
Costing or valuing the measure belongs to inventory-valuation-cogs.
Other writes, logging and measures outside the snapshot relation are reported, not reproduced.
A job that cannot be read or replayed is named unassessed, and its parity is stated unproven.
recipes.title: Convert a legacy periodic snapshot load into dbt and prove parity period by period
trigger: A scheduled job publishes one row per entity per period, such as stock on hand at each month-end, and the team wants it in dbt.
Consumers read the snapshot's history, so a move needs proof that every period still matches, not only the latest one.
Earlier periods are restated by late arrivals or corrections, or a period was never run, and nobody has written down what the legacy job does then.

recipes.description: Turn one approved small, static legacy reference table into a version-controlled dbt seed from an approved extract with a stated boundary, with typed columns, keys, tests and an ownership record, and prove the dbt consumers' output unchanged or changed only as approved; unsuitable tables are reported, not seeded.
recipes.pitch: Give a legacy lookup table to the dbt project as a seed, and show the reports that read it change only as you approve.
qualifiers: Needs the consuming dbt models to exist; moving them is another outcome.
Starts from an approved extract of the table with a stated boundary; it does not read the legacy database.
A table that keeps arriving as exports or grows belongs to an ingestion Recipe, not a seed.
Large or frequently changing tables are reported unsuitable, not seeded.
Retiring the legacy table or its writer is a separate approved step.
A table a routine derives from other data belongs to a writer-conversion Recipe, not a seed.
History to preserve belongs to dbt-snapshot-history; this seed holds the rows of the approved extract.
recipes.title: Move an approved legacy reference table into a dbt seed and prove downstream parity
trigger: A small, static lookup or code list that dbt models read lives in a legacy database, and its owner wants the dbt project to own it.
A legacy job still reloads a reference table that dbt models join, and nobody can say who may change it or what a change would do to the reports.
A migration plan marks a table as reference data, but nothing records that anyone approved it for seed ownership.
A table proposed as a seed may be too large or change too often, and needs a suitability decision before any file is made.

recipes.description: Scan the SQL files of a legacy repository at a named revision without changing them, index its tables, views, procedures and functions and the reads, writes and calls between them with source evidence, and report what cannot be resolved, the dependency order, blockers and candidate migration scopes.
recipes.pitch: Know what a legacy SQL repository holds and what depends on what, with evidence and honest gaps, before anyone picks a migration scope.
qualifiers: Planned until a product parser splits and classifies routine bodies and calls in T-SQL, PL/SQL and PL/pgSQL.
Reads files in the Intent's repository; a live database is inventory-legacy-database-over-mcp.
Fabric verdicts and a go or no-go for a Synapse or SSIS export belong to assess-synapse-ssis-for-fabric.
Stops at the index and candidate scopes; plans, dispositions, conversion and Intents are other Recipes.
Business-domain ownership of tables and views is not assigned; the index is an engineering input.
A dialect the scan cannot read is reported unparsed, never guessed or skipped.
Static reading cannot show runtime behaviour, string-built targets or objects created outside the repository.
recipes.title: Index a legacy SQL repository's objects and dependencies for migration planning
trigger: A legacy warehouse's SQL, or a DDL snapshot, is committed to a repository and nobody can say what objects exist or what depends on what before migration scope is chosen.
The team needs the tables, views, procedures and functions found, with what reads, writes or calls each, before it picks what to migrate first.
The repository holds duplicate definitions, objects with no definition, string-built SQL or files that do not parse, and the team needs them listed, not guessed.

recipes.description: Bring a legacy SQL script or view into dbt as models that publish the same contract, proven against the legacy logic's own output on the same inputs, with legacy defects reproduced and reported as follow-up work.
recipes.pitch: Retire a hand-run SQL script by rebuilding it in dbt and proving the new models return exactly what the old one did.
qualifiers: Needs the legacy output on the same inputs, from the legacy SQL or its current table.
Complete outcome assessed for duckdb_local only; the other listed platforms remain unassessed.
recipes.title: Convert a legacy SQL script or view into a dbt model and prove parity
trigger: A report or table is still produced by a hand-run SQL script or a database view outside dbt, with no tests, lineage or review.
The team wants to retire a legacy script, but its consumers need proof that the dbt version returns exactly the same rows.
Transformation logic written as step-by-step SQL (temp tables, updates, deletes) has to move into the dbt project.

recipes.description: Classify every loaded screening record as an enrolled subject, a screen failure with one named reason or a record set aside or left out of scope with its reason, and publish study, site and month enrollment against the approved target in force, with the approved screen-failure rate and time to first enrollment, tied back to the subjects.
recipes.pitch: Every screening record is enrolled, failed for a stated reason, set aside or left out of scope, and site performance ties back to the subjects.
qualifiers: Screening records and the site list with dates must be landed; reasons and targets may be captured as data.
Stops at enrollment and site performance; forecasting, site selection and monitoring are separate.
Screenings at sites missing from the data cannot be seen, and are not claimed absent.
recipes.title: Build clinical-trial enrollment and site-performance models with every screened subject accounted for
trigger: Clinical operations rebuilds enrollment and site performance in a spreadsheet each month, and nobody can say who was left out of the enrolled count or why a site looks slow.
Re-screens and people screened for more than one study are counted inconsistently, so enrolled counts and screen-failure rates cannot be defended.
Randomizations before a site was activated or after it closed, bad dates and subjects at unlisted sites sit in the counts or vanish from them without a trace.
A site that enrolled nobody in a month has no row, and a changed enrollment target is applied in the wrong period.

recipes.description: Build fleet utilisation with authoritative asset availability, maintenance-adjusted time, separate observation coverage and traceable numerator and denominator components that reconcile across daily and monthly reporting.
recipes.pitch: Measure fleet use against defensible available asset time while keeping missing observations and maintenance evidence visible.
recipes.title: Build fleet utilisation against explicit asset availability
trigger: A fleet dashboard labels observed vehicle occupancy as utilisation without an authoritative available-time denominator.
Fleet capacity reports omit available vehicles that never come online or subtract overlapping maintenance twice.
Daily and monthly vehicle utilisation disagree because roster, observation and downtime windows differ.

recipes.description: Build, for each approved lane and day, the transport trips due and how many arrived on time, early or late or remain open or overdue, with an on-time rate and lateness derived from trip events under the user's approved rules, and every unmeasurable record listed once with a reason as approved.
recipes.pitch: A lane-by-day on-time view built from trip events, with open trips, quiet lanes and unmeasurable records shown as approved.
qualifiers: Needs transport trips with a planned arrival and trip events with event times, already in the Domain.
Stops at lane-day punctuality; order-line in-full, freight cost, ETA forecasting and dwell are other outcomes.
A past as-of time reproduces only where event recorded times are kept; a rebuild restates it.
Exported files go to file-drop-to-bronze first.
recipes.title: Build lane-day on-time transport performance with open trips and exceptions shown as approved
trigger: A TMS dashboard reports on-time performance by lane, but nobody can inspect how it is calculated or reproduce its figure.
Trips that were due but never reported an arrival, or lanes that ran nothing on a day, drop out of the on-time figure.
A late arrival lands on a different day than planners expect, or time zones and clock changes move a trip's day or verdict.
Repeated or corrected events, cancelled trips and trips with no usable plan change the rate with no stated reason.

recipes.description: Replace a managed connector with an owned dlt pipeline landed side by side with the connector's tables, reconciled table by table over parallel runs with a cause for every difference, and stopped short of cutover.
recipes.pitch: Swap a Fivetran or Airbyte connector for a dlt pipeline you own, and prove table by table that it lands what the connector did before you cut over.
qualifiers: Needs read access to the connector's landed tables and to the source the connector reads.
Database sources need a dlt route Studio supports; its sql_database route is not supported today.
Complete outcome assessed for duckdb_local only; the other listed platforms remain unassessed.
recipes.title: Replace a Fivetran or Airbyte connector with a dlt pipeline and reconcile the result
trigger: A managed connector's bill changed shape, or it broke and the vendor fix has been pending for weeks, and the team wants the load in code it owns.
dbt models read a Fivetran or Airbyte connector's tables, so a replacement has to keep landing data those models can use.
Before switching off a managed connector, the team needs proof that its replacement lands the same records, with a reason for every difference.

recipes.description: Build availability, performance, quality and OEE per machine, shift and day with weighted line and plant roll-ups and a reason-ranked downtime Pareto, with every stop, count and machine accounted for.
recipes.pitch: Show what cost each line its OEE points with every stop, piece and machine accounted for.
qualifiers: Needs scheduled windows, a stop log, production counts and ideal cycle times
Stops at OEE and downtime ranking; yield and work-in-progress reconciliation are separate
Starts from reported stop intervals and period piece counts, not raw signals or counters
recipes.title: Build overall equipment effectiveness and a downtime Pareto
trigger: Plant OEE comes from a hand-built spreadsheet and nobody can say whether stops, slow running or scrap cost a line its points.
Line and plant OEE averages machine OEEs, so a small machine moves the number as much as a large one.
Stops with no reason, no end or a shift-change crossing distort availability and leave the downtime ranking unable to tie back to OEE.

recipes.description: From production orders, material issues and returns, operation completions, scrap, rework, split and merge records and finished-goods receipts, publish a movement ledger, work in progress per order and operation at approved cutoffs that reconciles under the approved identity and tolerance, first-pass and final yield, and every quantity that cannot be placed.
recipes.pitch: Reconcile every production-order movement into work in progress and yield, so a reworked unit counts once and every unplaced quantity stays visible.
qualifiers: Needs recorded movements per order and operation; planned or scheduled quantities never stand in for them.
Finding unexplained loss needs an observation such as counted work in progress; without one it is reported unproven.
Quantities only; costing, cost variances and equipment time are separate outcomes.
One output item per operation; co-products and by-products are a separate outcome.
Lot genealogy and recall exposure belong to inventory-lot-traceability.
Inputs are landed tables; loading files or extracts belongs to file-drop-to-bronze.
Holding a reported cutoff frozen, or showing what a restatement changed, needs kept source history or published rows.
A source with no recorded time cannot show late movements or status and routing changes; lateness is reported unproven.
recipes.title: Reconcile production-order movements into work in progress by operation, first-pass and final yield, and exceptions
trigger: Yield and work in progress come from a spreadsheet that counts a reworked unit as a second unit produced and cannot keep first-pass yield apart from final yield.
Opening work in progress plus what was started never equals closing work in progress, and nobody can say which operation lost the quantity.
Split, merge, scrap and finished-goods receipt records lose or double count quantity between operations of a production order.

recipes.description: From production orders, standard versions with their bills of material and routings, material issues, labour and machine time, other order costs, rates, overhead pools and good receipts, publish standard and actual cost per order and element at the approved cutoff, the approved variance effects, overhead absorbed so each pool ties, and every incomplete element or set-aside record.
recipes.pitch: Reconcile each production order's standard cost to actual by element, with every difference a named effect or a labelled exception and no rate made zero.
qualifiers: Needs standard versions, dated where the approved rule selects by date, with BOM, routing, prices and rates behind each.
Needs recorded issues, hours and receipts per order, and overhead pools; planned quantities never stand in for actuals.
One currency per run; translating currencies is upstream work.
Quantity flow, yield, and reconciling or valuing work in progress are separate outcomes.
Setting or rolling up standards, purchase price variance at receipt and ledger posting are separate outcomes.
Valuing inventory, finished goods and cost of goods sold belongs to inventory-valuation-cogs.
Co-products, by-products and joint-cost splits are a separate outcome.
Inputs are landed tables; loading files or extracts belongs to file-drop-to-bronze.
A source with no recorded time on postings, rates or pools cannot show late changes; restatement then reads unproven.
recipes.title: Reconcile production-order standard cost to actual by element, with variance effects, overhead absorption and exceptions
trigger: Production-order variances are worked out in a spreadsheet nobody can audit, and nobody can say which standard version each variance was measured against.
Actual cost differs from standard on an order and nobody can split the difference into price, usage, rate, efficiency and overhead effects.
Overhead is absorbed by hand, the amounts charged to orders never tie back to the cost-centre pool, and a missing labour rate or conversion factor quietly becomes zero.

recipes.description: From subcontract orders, approved components, transfers, returns, supplier reports, finished receipts and processing invoices, publish what is held at the subcontractor at the approved cutoff, the charge earned on delivered work with invoice lines matched to it, each supplier report compared with the approved quantity, and every exception.
recipes.pitch: Show what sits at the subcontractor, how its reports compare with approved usage, and whether its invoices match delivered work, every input accounted for.
qualifiers: Needs each order's approved components, quantity per finished unit, any allowance, its price basis and supplier.
Needs recorded transfers, returns, supplier reports, receipts with an accepted result, and invoice lines.
Covers components still company-owned at the subcontractor; buy-sell or consume-at-transfer is a separate outcome.
Supplier-reported figures never stand in for approved quantities unless the approved rule says so.
One subcontract process per order; chains of subcontract steps are a separate outcome.
One currency per order; translating currencies is upstream work.
Valuing components, WIP or COGS is inventory-valuation-cogs; purchased-goods matching is procurement-three-way-match.
A source with no recorded time cannot show late changes; restatement then reads unproven.
In-house production, standard cost, physical counts, supplier payment and ledger posting are separate outcomes.
Inputs are landed tables; loading files or extracts belongs to file-drop-to-bronze.
recipes.title: Reconcile components held at a subcontractor and processing charges to delivered work, with exceptions and coverage
trigger: Nobody can say how much of the company's material is sitting at a subcontractor, because transfers, returns, scrap reports and finished receipts live in different places and are never netted.
A subcontractor's processing invoice is paid or disputed without checking it against what was accepted, so unbilled work, over-billing and price differences go unseen.
A subcontractor reports its own consumption or scrap and nobody can compare it with what the approved bill of material allows for the finished parts received.

recipes.description: Declare the business objects behind the keys of the approved Ossie documents, each identified by its natural code, and map each key to the object it identifies. Leave version surrogates and derived hashes unmapped and named, and report every dataset keyed by an object no mapping names. Declaration only; no model changes.
recipes.pitch: Say which object every key identifies, and name every dataset keyed by an object nothing maps.
qualifiers: Needs Ossie documents already in the repository; writing them is the semantic-model Recipes' job.
A declaration only, so no mapping is executed and it stays unproven as a query until a consumer runs it.
Resolving one customer across systems is identity-golden-record-crosswalk, not this Recipe.
The ontology has no construct for a version of an object, so a key that names only a version stays unmapped.
recipes.title: Map each key to the business object it identifies across a Domain and find datasets keyed by an unmapped object
trigger: Several datasets carry customer, product or order keys, and nobody can say which business object a key identifies or whether two keys name the same one.
A key holds a version, a hash or a code and nothing records which, so a join on it counts a changed member twice or matches nothing.
A dataset is keyed by an object that no mapping names, and the gap shows only when someone asks where that object lives.

recipes.description: Compute fully loaded acquisition cost, customers acquired and cumulative contribution by acquisition cohort and channel under the user's approved rules, with a payback verdict per cohort and every cost and customer accounted for.
recipes.pitch: One reproducible cohort table that shows what each channel cost, what it has earned back and whether it has paid back, with shared cost counted once.
qualifiers: Needs dated cost lines, acquisition assignments, first-customer dates and contribution records.
Takes contribution, assignments and customer identity as given; the rules may be captured as editable data.
Keeps each currency separate unless an approved translation rule applies; rate sourcing is separate.
Reports attribution-based accounting to an as-of date; causal lift and forecasting are separate.
Stops at cohort cost and payback; touchpoint credit and lifetime value are separate outcomes.
recipes.title: Build fully loaded acquisition cost and contribution payback by customer cohort
trigger: Marketing says a channel pays back quickly and Finance says it never does, and nobody can show the sum from the spend and contribution records.
Shared campaign cost, agency and creative fees are counted in two channels or left out, so acquisition cost differs between reports.
A customer reassigned between campaigns, or a refund after payback, changes the answer and nobody can say whether the cohort has really recovered its cost.

recipes.description: Split the value of each qualifying conversion across the marketing touches before it under several approved attribution models side by side, with each model's credit adding back to the conversion value, every touch and conversion accounted for, and channels compared across models.
recipes.pitch: One reproducible attribution whose credit under every model adds back to booked value, so teams can see exactly where they differ.
qualifiers: Touchpoint, conversion and any adjustment records must already be landed as tables; this Recipe does not ingest them.
Who converted is resolved through the identity the Intent supplies; this Recipe does not build identity.
Visits or sessions used as touches must already be built; this Recipe does not sessionize events.
Rule-based models only; data-driven models, incrementality, spend and payback are out of scope.
recipes.title: Attribute conversions to touchpoints under several models side by side
trigger: Marketing and Sales each have a spreadsheet crediting their channel with the same revenue, and together they claim more than was booked.
Channel credit differs between tools or reports and nobody can show which rule explains the gap.
A lookback, conversion or model setting is about to change and the owner must see which channels gain or lose, and why, before the numbers move.

recipes.description: Build a campaign-day plan and actual ledger as of each approved reporting cutoff, with the approved budget revision at that cutoff, provisional and settled cost kept apart, remaining budget and eligible delivery days left, and campaign totals that reconcile to the portfolio at every cutoff.
recipes.pitch: A point-in-time pacing ledger where each cutoff keeps its own approved plan and every cost, credit and set-aside reconciles to the portfolio.
qualifiers: Needs recorded times on revisions, pauses, spend, bills, adjustments, versioned flights; past knowledge is not rebuilt.
Flights, revisions, spend and bills arrive as landed tables; ingesting them is a separate outcome.
Reporting only; bid changes, forecasts and acquisition payback are separate outcomes.
recipes.title: Build a campaign-day budget pacing ledger against versioned flight plans
trigger: Campaign owners ask whether a campaign is on pace and the answer changes with which budget version and which cost number someone used.
A mid-flight budget change rewrote last month's plan, so nobody can show what was approved at the time.
Platform spend is restated after the day and billed credits arrive late, and marketing finance cannot tell provisional cost from settled cost.

recipes.description: Decide, for each planned contact at a reporting cutoff, whether it is included or suppressed under the user's approved caps, window, priority and consent rules, with a reason when suppressed, the contacts already used against each cap, its rank where ranked, and every input row accounted for.
recipes.pitch: One auditable send-eligibility table that counts each delivery once, ranks competing contacts the same way every run and says why a contact was held back.
qualifiers: Needs planned contacts, reported contact events with times, an identifier-to-person map and a published consent state.
Takes consent state and person identity as given; consent derivation and identity resolution are separate outcomes.
Publishes eligibility data only; sending, scheduling, quiet hours and journey logic are separate.
Gives no legal advice; caps and consent rules are the user's, not a compliance finding.
A source with no event-time field stops the run; a row with a missing time follows the approved rule.
recipes.title: Build cross-channel contact-pressure and send-eligibility decisions for planned contacts
trigger: The same person is emailed, texted and pushed by several tools in one week, and nobody can say whether the next planned contact is allowed.
One delivery reported by two tools is counted twice, or a contact exactly at the edge of the rolling window is counted differently in each report.
Two contacts planned for one person at the same moment are ordered by load order, so a different one wins each run.
A planned contact has no consent record or no identifiable person, and it is sent or silently dropped with no reason.

recipes.description: Resolve accounts to their parent and ultimate parent under approved precedence and parent rules, keep accounts the rules cannot place explicitly unresolved unless an approved fallback places them, roll measures up every level of each corporate family for the approved periods, and list every hierarchy anomaly with its reason, never double counting an account or inventing hierarchy.
recipes.pitch: See every corporate family's total, with every account placed or explicitly unresolved and every broken parent link explained.
qualifiers: Families as they stood in past periods need dated parent-link history; without it they cannot be rebuilt.
Accounts must already be one record per company; this Recipe does not deduplicate accounts.
Complete outcome assessed for duckdb_local only; the other listed platforms remain unassessed.
recipes.title: Resolve B2B account hierarchies and roll measures to the ultimate parent
trigger: Sales and finance cannot see total revenue or pipeline for a whole corporate family because subsidiaries sit as separate accounts.
The CRM's parent-account field has gaps, loops and conflicts with a firmographic vendor, and nobody knows which link to trust.
After an acquisition or divestiture, reports disagree on which family a past month's revenue belongs to.
Named-account or territory rules apply at the ultimate-parent level and need each account mapped to its parent and ultimate parent.

recipes.description: Bind every source item to at most one conformed product and SKU or list why not, map each source category into the approved conformed hierarchy with each product placed at most once per view or listed unplaced, and tie item counts and units to each source at every level with every difference explained or marked not tied.
recipes.pitch: One conformed catalog, every item bound or explained, every product rolled up once, and totals that tie back to each source.
qualifiers: Item records, category trees and any sale lines must already be landed as tables; this Recipe does not ingest catalogs.
An item no approved rule can bind stays unbound unless an approved cross-reference binds it.
Units tie out only for systems that supply sale lines.
Earlier taxonomy versions can be rebuilt only from dated mapping history; without it they cannot be restated.
recipes.title: Conform product and SKU hierarchies across systems
trigger: The same product carries different SKUs and category trees in the ERP, the web shop and the point of sale, so sales by category disagree between reports.
A new system or an acquisition brings another catalog and nobody can say which of its items are already known.
Category reporting needs one taxonomy with each product in exactly one place, and duplicate or reused SKUs and GTINs make product counts untrustworthy.

recipes.description: Bring a materialized view into dbt as a model that publishes the same contract and computes each refresh under the same approved rule, proven against the view's own output after each compared refresh, with view defects reproduced and reported as follow-up work.
recipes.pitch: Retire a materialized view by rebuilding it in dbt and proving each compared refresh matches the view's.
qualifiers: Needs the view's definition (Studio can't yet read it on these targets), refresh rule and output at refresh points.
Not yet assessed end to end on fabric_lakehouse, redshift or databricks.
recipes.title: Convert a materialized view into a dbt model and preserve its required refresh semantics
trigger: Warehouse logic lives in a materialized view that nobody can test, review or trace, and the team wants it in the dbt project.
Consumers depend on what each refresh of the view produces, so the dbt model must keep what every refresh computes, not only its final rows.
The view's refresh is opaque, and the team wants its refresh rule stated and owned in code before the view is retired.

recipes.description: Implement a metric with approved eligibility, numerator and denominator components, missing-value and zero-denominator policies, weighting, dimension coverage and verified rollups at supported grains.
recipes.pitch: Make the metric's population and components explicit so its values and supported totals can be checked.
recipes.title: Build a metric with explicit eligibility and reconcilable rollups
trigger: A new percentage, rate or average needs a defensible eligible population and missing-value policy.
Daily and monthly metrics disagree, or totals change when a report groups the same records differently.
Trip tips, vehicle occupancy or delivery service rates depend on eligibility, measurement coverage and weighting.

recipes.description: Author a MotherDuck Flight as committed code that runs the approved load and then the dbt build of an approved selection on a schedule, under approved failure, recovery and overlap rules, prove its order, failure paths and carried project against the committed program, and run it in a MotherDuck sandbox where approved.
recipes.pitch: Replace the laptop cron with a committed MotherDuck Flight that loads, builds and fails loudly on a schedule.
qualifiers: Schedules the load and build on MotherDuck only; local DuckDB has no scheduler.
The dbt project the Flight carries must fit MotherDuck's Flight source-code size limit.
A schedule only runs on a MotherDuck plan that offers scheduled Flight runs.
The load must reach its source from the Flight runtime, with credentials held as Flight secrets.
Scheduling on Fabric belongs to fabric-data-pipeline-as-code.
Not yet assessed end to end on motherduck.
recipes.title: Schedule a dlt load and a dbt build on MotherDuck as a committed MotherDuck Flight
trigger: The MotherDuck load and the dbt build that follows it run from a cron job on someone's laptop.
A dlt load and a dbt build on MotherDuck have to run in order on a schedule without standing up an orchestrator.
A scheduled run reports success while the load or the build behind it actually failed.

recipes.description: Port an existing dbt project to a new destination and compare each relation in the approved scope with the unchanged project over identical inputs, within approved equality rules, with every destination-specific construct accounted for and a cutover recommendation that names what is still open.
recipes.pitch: Find out whether a dbt project returns the same results on its new destination, within rules you approve, before anyone cuts over.
qualifiers: Needs a second engine executable from the Intent; a same-engine rehearsal cannot show an engine difference.
recipes.title: Move a dbt project to a new destination and check parity before cutover
trigger: A dbt project has to run on a different warehouse or lakehouse, and the dashboards and reports that read it cannot show a different number afterwards.
Someone says the migration is done because the build is green on the new destination, but nobody has compared what consumers read.
The project uses functions, types, hooks or access rules that may not exist or behave the same on the new destination.
The team needs a go or no-go for cutover, with the open items named.

recipes.description: Bring a hand-run notebook transformation into dbt as models that publish the same contract, proven against what the unchanged notebook writes on the same inputs, with its implicit dataframe behaviour and defects reproduced and reported as follow-up work.
recipes.pitch: Retire a hand-run notebook by rebuilding its dataframe logic in dbt and proving the new models publish what the notebook did.
qualifiers: Needs the notebook's output on the same inputs, from a run of the unchanged notebook or its current table.
Complete outcome assessed for duckdb_local only; the other listed platforms remain unassessed.
recipes.title: Convert a notebook transformation into a dbt model and prove parity
trigger: A table or report is still produced by running a notebook by hand, pulling warehouse data into dataframes, with no tests, lineage or review.
The team wants the notebook's logic in the dbt project, but its consumers need proof that the dbt version returns the same results.
Dataframe code (merges, group-bys, fills, de-duplication, pivots) has to move into dbt models without changing what the notebook published.

recipes.description: Build evidence-backed state and location intervals, split them across agreed reporting boundaries, and reconcile durations with explicit unknown periods, missing closes and source lineage.
recipes.pitch: Explain how long each entity spent in a state and where, without inventing locations or filling unknown time with activity.
recipes.title: Build state durations by entity, location and reporting period
trigger: Waiting, idle, available or busy time must be measured by site or zone and hour from operational event histories.
State and location change independently, leaving reports unable to explain where an entity spent its time.
Vehicle or equipment events have missing closes or observation gaps that could inflate operational duration totals.

recipes.description: At the approved grain and count date, set warehouse, ERP and count quantities side by side in one unit, give each pair of systems its own difference and reason under approved rules, keep what no rule explains visible, and account for every record of every input.
recipes.pitch: Put three inventory systems side by side and give every difference a reason, with nothing quietly absorbed.
qualifiers: A timing reason needs a movement log and evidence the approved rule accepts of which system lagged.
Quantities only; valuation, availability promising and consignment ownership settlement are separate outcomes.
Inputs are landed tables; loading files or extracts belongs to file-drop-to-bronze.
Stops at the classified reconciliation; posting adjustments back to a system is a separate outcome.
Reproducing a past count date after rule or source changes needs kept history of the sources.
Assessed end to end on duckdb_local only; the other listed targets rely on dbt support and are unassessed.
recipes.title: Reconcile inventory positions across warehouse, ERP and physical counts and give every difference a reason
trigger: The warehouse system, the ERP and the last stock count report different quantities for the same item and nobody can say which is right or why.
A stock count is due and the variance report is a spreadsheet that cannot tell a counting error from a timing difference or a posting error.
Finance asks why book inventory differs from what is on the shelf before the books close.

recipes.description: For each approved as-of date, judge every in-scope order line on time, in full and both under the user's approved promise, tolerance and partial-shipment rules, give each miss one reason, roll the verdicts up by order, customer, carrier and plant from the lines, and keep every excluded record visible with its reason.
recipes.pitch: One delivery figure per order line, order, customer, carrier and plant, with a reason for every miss and nothing dropped.
qualifiers: Needs order lines (promise date, quantity) and shipment legs (dates, quantities, plus plant and carrier for the cuts).
Stops at delivery verdicts and cuts; freight cost, carrier contracts, forecasting and inventory are separate outcomes.
A past as-of date reproduces only from kept promise and cancellation history; a rebuild restates it.
Order and shipment tables already in the Domain; exported files go to file-drop-to-bronze first.
Assessed end to end on duckdb_local only; the other listed targets rely on dbt support and are unassessed.
recipes.title: Measure on-time-in-full delivery by customer, carrier and plant
trigger: Customers report late deliveries, and Sales, Supply Chain and the carriers each quote a different on-time-in-full figure because each applies its own promise date, tolerance and partial-shipment rule.
A late or short order cannot be traced to a plant, a carrier or a customer change, so each side blames another.
A shipment is split across days, carriers or plants, or the customer moved the promise date, and no report says whether the line counted as on time, in full or neither.
Cancelled lines, lines not yet due, undelivered lines and shipments matching no order line fall out of the delivery figure with no stated reason.

recipes.description: For the approved periods, roll invoice lines up to a spend cube, match each line to the contract that governs it and flag it on or off contract with the approved reason, keeping every line, credit and unmatched record visible so no spend is lost, counted twice or silently cleared.
recipes.pitch: Build one defensible monthly spend cube and see which lines were bought off contract, and why, line by line.
qualifiers: Invoice lines, purchase-order lines and contracts arrive as landed tables; landing them is a separate outcome.
Supplier identity and item categories arrive conformed; matching suppliers and mapping items are separate outcomes.
Stops at the cube and contract flags; aging, duplicates, three-way match, rebates and savings are separate outcomes.
Without an approved contract-exempt list, spend with no contract on file is unproven, not non-compliant.
Currency conversion needs an approved rate source; without one, other-currency lines are shown apart from the totals.
Assessed end to end on duckdb_local only; the other listed targets rely on dbt support and are unassessed.
recipes.title: Build the procurement spend cube and flag invoice lines on or off contract
trigger: Procurement, Finance and the business units each quote a different spend total, and nobody can say how much was bought outside a contract.
Procurement is asked which suppliers and categories are bought off contract and why, and cannot show the invoice lines behind the number.
A contract expires or is renegotiated and the team cannot see how much spend still flows to it after the end date, above its price or beyond its cap.

recipes.description: Build order-line economics that separate refund value, returned quantity, recoverable goods cost, fees, fulfilment and return handling into a margin, with order and period rollups that reconcile to the lines and show where margin is unknown.
recipes.pitch: Show what an order actually earned after refunds, returns and recovered stock, with every adjustment counted once and no missing cost hidden as zero.
qualifiers: Needs order-line, refund and return records; costs may be captured as approved editable data.
recipes.title: Build order-line contribution margin with order and period rollups after refunds and returns
trigger: Gross sales minus original item cost overstates order margin because refunds and returns arrive after the order.
Finance cannot explain a margin because refund value, returned stock, recovered inventory cost, fees and return handling are mixed or missing.
A refund is delivered twice, a return is partial, or a refund has no physical return, and the order margin moves the wrong way.

recipes.description: Classify every leaver, compute attrition rates for the approved cuts under the user's approved definitions, show how tenure is spread across current staff and how each hire cohort is retained, and reconcile leavers to the headcount roll-forward, while every termination record stays accounted for and small groups stay hidden where the approved policy hides them.
recipes.pitch: One attrition, tenure and retention picture built on the same people the headcount counts, with every leaver accounted for.
qualifiers: Needs per-worker period-end state with population status (and FTE if the base uses it) and its roll-forward.
Needs termination records with a date, a reason code and the worker's placement on the last day worked.
Results as known on a past date need kept snapshots; backdated HR changes restate past periods.
Stops at attrition, tenure and retention; building headcount, pay and forecasting are separate outcomes.
Assessed end to end on duckdb_local only; the other listed targets rely on dbt support and are unassessed.
recipes.title: Measure attrition, tenure and hire-cohort retention from the headcount outputs
trigger: Leadership asks whether attrition is rising and where, and nobody can answer from one consistent set of figures.
HR and finance quote different turnover rates for the same year because each counts leavers and headcount differently.
Nobody can say whether recent hires leave faster than earlier ones, or how long people stay before they go.

recipes.description: From effective-dated job history, place every worker in the approved population at each reporting date, publish headcount and FTE at the approved grain with org roll-ups, explain each period's change through approved movement classes, and keep every excluded or unprocessable record visible so no worker is lost or counted twice.
recipes.pitch: Turn effective-dated HR job history into one month-end headcount and FTE everyone can use, with a roll-forward that ties every period.
qualifiers: Past headcount needs effective-dated job history; a current-state worker table cannot show past moves.
Reproducing figures as known on a past date needs entry timestamps or kept snapshots of the results.
Stops at headcount, FTE and the roll-forward; attrition, tenure, payroll and positions are separate.
Assessed end to end on duckdb_local only; the other listed targets rely on dbt support and are unassessed.
recipes.title: Build period-end headcount and FTE by org and a roll-forward that ties every period
trigger: HR, finance and the board deck each report a different headcount for the same month-end, and nobody can say why.
Every month someone rebuilds opening plus hires minus leavers plus transfers in a spreadsheet, and it never equals the closing headcount.
Leadership asks how many people a team had at a past month-end, under the org structure that applied then.

recipes.description: For the approved review date, place each counted worker's pay against the band in force, keep that worker-level result apart from the published outputs, and publish only approved aggregates, such as unadjusted pay gaps, with the approved small-group hiding, while every record is accounted for.
recipes.pitch: Check pay against salary bands and publish approved pay gaps by group, with approved small-group hiding and its remaining limits stated.
qualifiers: Pay, band and worker records arrive as landed tables; landing them is a separate outcome.
Stops at the check and the aggregate report; remediation, adjusted-gap modelling and pay planning are separate outcomes.
Restricting worker-level pay needs roles and grants (pii-classification-and-masking); without them it is a label.
On fabric_lakehouse, SQL grants do not govern OneLake reads, so restriction cannot be assured there.
Statutory report formats and statistical significance are separate outcomes.
Hiding small groups alone does not make a figure safe to release; totals and other releases can reveal one.
Unless issued reports are frozen, a later correction restates them; frozen ones need kept snapshots.
Assessed end to end on duckdb_local only; the other listed targets rely on dbt support and are unassessed.
recipes.title: Check pay against salary bands and report pay gaps at an aggregate grain
trigger: A pay-equity review is due and worker-level compensation cannot be shared widely.
Managers are told people are paid outside the band, but nobody can say how many, where, or on which band version.
HR is asked for pay gaps between groups and cannot tell whether publishing a number could reveal a small group.

recipes.description: At the approved reconciliation grain, set the payroll register total, mapped to GL accounts, beside what the ledger posted, explain the difference as breaks classed under approved rules, leave any residual visible as unexplained, and account for every register line and ledger posting.
recipes.pitch: Reconcile payroll to the ledger at every cut-off with each break classified and nothing quietly absorbed.
qualifiers: Needs a pay-code mapping to GL accounts, supplied or agreed; the Recipe never infers one.
Linking postings to pay runs needs a run reference on the ledger or an approved matching rule.
Reproducing a past tie-out after rule or source changes needs kept history of the tie-out.
Stops at the classified tie-out; payroll calculation, correcting journals and sign-off are separate outcomes.
Payroll registers keyed by pay run; document-linked control accounts belong to finance-gl-subledger-tieout.
Assessed end to end on duckdb_local only; the other listed targets rely on dbt support and are unassessed.
recipes.title: Tie payroll to the general ledger at every cut-off and classify every break
trigger: Payroll expense in the general ledger does not match the payroll register at close, and the gap is worked out by hand.
Finance cannot say which pay run or cost center explains the difference between the register and the ledger.
An auditor asks what an accrual, an off-cycle run or a misposting did to a period, and someone has to rebuild the answer.

recipes.description: Classify every column of the governed relations as a kind of personal data or as not personal, serve a lower-privilege audience each kind masked as approved, limit that audience to the approved access, prove the masked outputs correct whether or not grants are applied, and, where applying the grants is approved, verify each role's effective access, including whether clear values can be recovered.
recipes.pitch: Classify personal data by column, mask it by kind for a lower-privilege audience, and verify that audience's access where grants are applied.
qualifiers: Needs database roles or groups and per-object grants on the target; DuckDB and MotherDuck have neither.
Applying the roles and grants and running the role checks need a live warehouse and approval to change access.
Fabric Lakehouse is excluded because its SQL endpoint grants do not govern OneLake or Spark reads.
Assumes the lower-privilege audience has no storage-level read path that bypasses database grants.

A data science team wants one row per entity and prediction time with a forward label, and no proof that each feature used only what was known by then.

recipes.description: Move the preparation of selected Power Query outputs into dbt models over landed source tables, with a verdict for every step, each output compared with a reference refresh on an agreed window, the points where M and SQL part ways reported, and a cutover and recovery plan that keeps the workbook untouched.

recipes.description: From purchase order line history, build each line's outstanding quantity and value at each approved reporting cutoff under the approved discharge rule, explain every movement from the previous cutoff, show received-not-invoiced goods as approved, and account for every record that moves nothing, shown or counted with its reason as approved.

recipes.title: Build the open purchase commitment balance and a roll-forward that explains every cutoff

After a partial receipt, an amendment or a cancel-and-reopen, nobody can say how much of an order line is still committed or why the balance moved.
An invoice, a receipt reversal or a return arrives and the open balance is relieved twice or not at all.

recipes.description: For the approved period, compare approved baseline prices with the quantities and prices actually invoiced to build a ledger that classifies each claimed saving under the approved classes, such as realized, negotiated but not realized, cost avoidance, currency effect, price increase or unsupported, with every invoice line accounted for.

States a price difference from the approved baseline, never that procurement caused it.
recipes.title: Reconcile negotiated procurement savings to realized invoice prices in a traceable savings ledger

recipes.description: Place purchases under the approved agreement version, net approved returns, compute each contract period's rebate entitlement under the approved tier method, and publish an accrual and settlement ledger that rolls forward, with every in-scope record that accrues or settles nothing listed and what the scope leaves out shown or counted as approved.
recipes.pitch: See what each supplier owes you under each approved contract, how it moved and what suppliers have already credited.

Stops at the contract-based amount; spend cubes, invoice matching, usage charges and forecasts are separate.
Accrues the rebate earned on purchases made so far; it does not project where a contract period will end.
Returns and credits link to a purchase line or agreement by an explicit reference or an approved linking rule.

A rebate term the approved rule form cannot express is listed as unmodelled, never ignored.
Without recorded dates on versions, returns or credits, their period placement is reported unproven.
recipes.title: Accrue supplier rebates from purchasing contracts and reconcile settlements
trigger: Procurement cannot say how much supplier rebate has been earned under each purchasing agreement this period, or how much of it suppliers have already credited.
Tiered agreements, returns and agreement changes are worked out by hand, so nobody can tell why an accrual moved or whether a supplier credit was counted twice.
Finance books a rebate receivable that does not tie to the agreements, because returns, restated agreements or an over-paid credit are missing from it.

recipes.description: For the approved review date, match each purchase order line to its receipts and invoices under the approved quantity, price and unit rules, show what it settles to and what is pending, and keep every source line and every exception visible so nothing is matched beyond what the approved rules allow, lost or counted twice.
recipes.pitch: See what each purchase order line settles to against goods received and invoiced, with every exception listed before anyone pays.

Stops at the match; spend cubes, duplicate invoice detection and recovering overpayments are separate.
Receipts and invoices link to a purchase order line by an explicit reference or an approved linking rule.
recipes.title: Match purchase orders, receipts and invoices line by line with an exception ledger
trigger: Accounts payable is asked to release payment and cannot say how much of an invoice is covered by the goods actually received.
One purchase order line has several receipts and several invoices, and nobody can tell which receipt covers which invoice.
Receipts reversed, goods returned, credit notes and different units leave the purchase order, receipt and invoice systems disagreeing, and the differences sit in spreadsheets.

recipes.description: Resolve landed batch event exports to identities and visits, build a funnel from configured steps, account for every event, and reproduce a reference figure with each difference attributed to a named cause.

recipes.title: Sessionize event streams and build reproducible funnels from batch exports

Session or conversion counts change between runs or when a late or overlapping export batch arrives.
Teams define a visit or a conversion differently, and a funnel step cannot be traced back to events.

recipes.description: Produce an independent assessment of an existing dbt change against approved requirements and baselines, with semantic checks, evidence gaps and a merge recommendation while preserving the reviewed implementation.

A reviewer must distinguish an implementation defect from missing data, missing relationships or insufficient test coverage.

recipes.description: For the approved awards, categories and periods, publish authorized, obligated, expended and drawn amounts with unobligated balance, unliquidated obligations and cash position, dated changes applied as approved, exceptions flagged beside the figures, and every source line counted, de-obligated or set aside with a reason.

recipes.title: Track grant funds per award from authorization to drawdown and flag exceptions

recipes.description: Publish one boundary data contract on each re-engineered gold table in the approved scope, drafted from the built table and checked against the legacy output it replaced, read over MCP without changing the source, with every difference and doubt queued and, where the owner approves, the contracts enforced in the build.

recipes.title: Publish boundary data contracts on re-engineered gold tables and queue what the legacy output leaves open

recipes.description: At the approved dates and grains, publish stock by owner at each store and SKU with owned and consigned stock kept apart, the supplier obligation the approved liability event creates, reverses and settles, one movement ledger tying units and amounts to both, and every input record accounted for.

recipes.description: At each approved settlement cutoff, publish each order line's sale, refunds, fees, chargebacks and reserve movements, each order's and account's paid, held, adjusted, pending and outstanding amounts, and each payout batch's tie to what it carries, with every difference visible and every unplaceable record listed with its reason.

recipes.title: Reconcile marketplace orders to net payouts and held reserves by order line and settlement cutoff

Reports the cash the records show, not why a till is short.
Settles the counted drawer; cashier attribution is separate.

recipes.description: Describe the approved existing dbt marts as a governed Ossie semantic model, with each table's row grain and how its numbers roll up. recipes.description: For each approved as-of date, tie every in-scope booking line to what was scheduled, billed after credit memos and collected, split each gap into breaks classed under the user's approved rules, show any residual as unexplained, and keep every unplaceable record visible with its reason.

recipes.title: Tie bookings to billings to cash and classify every break

trigger: Reps, managers and finance disagree on attainment because each team credits bookings with its own spreadsheet logic.

Plan rates changed mid-year and the team cannot say which version priced which booking.

Forecast and bookings totals disagree because deals slipped, were never forecast or were cancelled, and nobody can say how much of the gap each explains.

Missing or conflicting conversion links are guessed or dropped, so the funnel cannot be audited back to its source rows.

recipes.description: Build per-ticket response and resolution SLA outcomes from ticket status, priority, team and reply history under approved targets, calendars, pauses, reopens and policy versions, then derive attainment by period, priority and team, a daily open-backlog age view and an exceptions list that accounts for every ticket, with an optional vendor comparison when ticket-level vendor results exist.

recipes.title: Track ticket SLA attainment and backlog aging outside the vendor dashboard

SLA attainment must be reported by period, priority and team under the support team's own hours, pauses and reopen rules.
A breach must be traceable to the business hours, pauses and policy version that applied to that ticket.

recipes.description: Publish one date table, one row per day without gaps over an approved window, carrying calendar attributes, fiscal year, period, quarter and week, a business-day flag and a prior-year pointer under approved rules, with unplaceable dates handled as approved.

recipes.title: Build one shared calendar and fiscal-period date table

Facts dated outside the date table, or with no date, silently drop out of the reports that join it.

recipes.title: Normalize multi-currency amounts to a reporting currency with as-of rates

A rate was corrected after the fact and nobody can say whether a past figure used the old rate or the corrected one.

recipes.description: Build shift-grain revenue, cost and margin components from defensible event assignments and approved cost allocations, with visible cost completeness and reconciled driver, vehicle and period rollups.

Shift margins disagree with driver, vehicle or period totals, or low-exposure shifts dominate a ranking.

recipes.description: Give every source table a dbt project declares a freshness limit, or a recorded exemption, and gate the builds that run the check so a source past its fail limit holds back the work the approved failure policy names before it rebuilds, with a report of each table's age, its limit and the work held back.

recipes.description: Rebuild the pivots, subtotals, recursive hierarchies and generated keys of a legacy reporting query in dbt, reading the source over MCP without changing it, with each construct mapped to a target form, shown equal to the legacy result or different only as approved, and legacy defects reported, not fixed.

recipes.description: Turn usage events, with repeats and revisions resolved under approved rules, and approved contract terms into charge lines per customer, period, meter and currency with allowance, tier method and credits applied, every event accounted for, and corrections restated for only the affected scope.
